{{short description|Statistics program by the NFL }}
[[File:NFL NGS Logo.png|thumb|The logo for Next Gen Stats]]
'''Next Generation Stats''', or simply '''Next Gen Stats''' ('''NGS'''), refers to data collected by the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and the advanced statistics drawn from that data. Going beyond the standard statistics recorded in NFL games (such as passing yards, rushing touchdowns, or interceptions), NGS data instead focuses on advanced statistics, with raw data collected being used to "automate player participation reports, calculate performance metrics, and derive advanced statistics".<ref name=ops/> 

==History==
The 2011 [[NFL collective bargaining agreement]] saw players agree to having their on-field location and health metrics tracked.<ref name=Savov>{{cite web|last=Savov|first=Vlad|url=https://www.theverge.com/2014/10/28/7082683/nfl-real-time-motion-tracking-by-zebra-technologies|title= How the NFL tracks everything on the field but the ball |work=[[The Verge]]|date=October 28, 2014|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref> Next Gen Stats was developed by the NFL in partnership with [[Zebra Technologies]] and [[Wilson Sporting Goods]].<ref name=ops>{{cite web|url=https://operations.nfl.com/gameday/technology/nfl-next-gen-stats/|title=NFL Next Gen Stats|publisher=[[National Football League|NFL Football Operations]]|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref> The former is the NFL's official player tracking partner, with the partnership beginning in 2014.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kern|first=Tyler|url=https://marketscale.com/industries/sports-and-entertainment/meet-the-company-behind-the-nfls-next-gen-stats/|title= Meet the Company Behind the NFL's Next Gen Stats |work=MarketScale|date=August 16, 2021|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Belzer|first=Jason|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/jasonbelzer/2014/07/31/nfl-partners-with-zebra-technologies-to-provide-next-generation-player-tracking/?sh=6a7950955598|title=NFL Partners With Zebra Technologies To Provide Next Generation Player Tracking|work=[[Forbes (magazine)|Forbes]]|date=July 31, 2014|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref> NGS data collection runs on [[Amazon Web Services]] (AWS) infrastructure, as well.<ref name=ops/> NGS are recorded using sensors worn by players during each game.<ref name=BW/> An example of raw data collected by NGS includes a [[wide receiver]]'s real-time speed, acceleration, and route paths are tracked by Next Gen.<ref name=BW/>

Zebra described 2014 as a "best effort" year, with [[2014 NFL season|that season]] seeing the introduction of location beacons embedded in each player's shoulder pads, as well as referees and [[first down]] measuring sticks also being equipped with [[radio-frequency identification]] (RFID) tags.<ref name=Savov/> Zebra's MotionWorks RFID system  was installed in 18 NFL stadiums during the 2014 season to track vector data.<ref>{{cite web|last=Moynihan|first=Tim|url=https://www.wired.com/2015/08/nfl-players-getting-rfid-chips-season/|title=All NFL Players Are Getting RFID Chips This Season|work=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]|date=August 7, 2015|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref>  At the time, there was a half-second latency and a margin of error of less than six inches; the ball was noted by ''[[The Verge]]'' as the only "untracked entity on the field".<ref name=Savov/> They worked on a custom transmitter with a wider weight distribution. Eventually, [[List of current NFL stadiums|every NFL venue]] had a tracker system installed, composed of: "20–30 ultra-wide band receivers, 2–3 [[radio-frequency identification]] (RFID) tags installed into the players' shoulder pads, and RFID tags on officials, [[End zone|pylons]], sticks, [[Chain crew|chains]], and in the ball".<ref name=ops/>

In 2015, [[Microsoft]] included "Next Gen Replay" as a feature on its NFL [[mobile app]] for the [[Xbox One]] and [[Windows 10]] devices.<ref>{{cite web|last=Baig|first=Edward C.|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/tech/columnist/baig/2015/08/07/microsoft-nfl-next-gen-stats/31271297/|title=Microsoft's new game plan for the NFL: Next-gen stats, Surface replays|work=[[USA Today]]|date=August 7, 2015|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Olavsrud|first=Thor|url=https://www.cio.com/article/245058/the-internet-of-things-comes-to-the-nfl.html|title=The Internet of Things comes to the NFL|work=[[CIO (magazine)|CIO]]|date=September 7, 2015|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref> NFL.com writers have referred to seasons since [[2016 NFL season|2016]] as the "Next Gen era".<ref>{{cite web|last=Holzman-Escareno|first=Anthony|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/new-trend-alert-for-nfl-offenses-ranking-top-five-pass-catching-groups|title= NFL stats and records, Week 13: Jalen Hurts breaks multiple Eagles records in win over Titans |website=[[NFL.com]]|date=December 5, 2022|accessdate=October 11, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Brooks|first=Bucky|author-link=Bucky Brooks|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/new-trend-alert-for-nfl-offenses-ranking-top-five-pass-catching-groups|title= New trend alert for NFL offenses; ranking top five pass-catching groups |website=[[NFL.com]]|date=May 10, 2024|accessdate=October 11, 2024}}</ref>

NGS developed a new passing metric in 2022, aimed to convey a passer's contributions better than similar metrics such as [[passer rating]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Aubet|first1=Francois-Xavier|last2=Ehrlich|first2=Elena|url=https://www.amazon.science/blog/the-science-behind-nfl-next-gen-stats-new-passing-metric|title= The science behind NFL Next Gen Stats' new passing metric |work=[[Amazon (company)|Amazon Science]]|date=August 26, 2022|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref> [[Machine learning]] tools are used as part of AWS' role in NGS data collection, helping generate new metrics, such as the 2024 introductions of the "Tackle Probability" and "Offensive Shift and Motion Classification" stats.<ref>{{cite web|last=Entin|first=Ari|url=https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/media/a-new-take-on-tackling-nfl-next-gen-stats-and-aws-bring-data-to-the-gridiron/|title=A new take on tackling: NFL Next Gen Stats and AWS bring data to the gridiron|work=AWS for M&E Blog|publisher=[[Amazon (company)|Amazon]]|date=September 10, 2024|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref><ref name=NGS2024>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/next-gen-stats-new-advanced-metrics-you-need-to-know-for-the-2024-nfl-season|title= Next Gen Stats: New advanced metrics you NEED to know for the 2024 NFL season |work=Next Gen Stats|publisher=[[National Football League]]|date=September 4, 2024|accessdate=October 10, 2024}}</ref>

The NFL's broadcast partners, of which [[Amazon Prime Video]] is one, utilize and reference Next Gen Stats in their broadcasts.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kleen|first=Brendon|url=https://awfulannouncing.com/nfl/nfl-broadcasts-next-gen-stats-record.html|title=NFL broadcasts are using Next Gen Stats way more this year than ever before|work=Awful Announcing|date=December 14, 2023|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref> [[CBS]], for example, has used Next Gen Stats in their "RomoVision" visuals on ''[[NFL on CBS]]'' broadcasts.<ref>{{cite web|last=Lemire|first=Joe|url=https://www.sportsbusinessjournal.com/Daily/Issues/2021/12/23/Technology/cbss-romovision-technology-in-collaboration-with-next-gen-stats-and-second-spectrum-is-the-future-of-tv-sportsstarting-right-now.aspx|title=CBS' RomoVision Technology, in Collaboration With Next Gen Stats and Second Spectrum, Is the Future of TV Sports—Starting Right Now|work=[[Sports Business Journal]]|date=December 23, 2021|accessdate=October 17, 2024}}</ref> NGS data has been cited by sports media outlets such as [[ESPN]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/41593254/nfl-week-5-2024-questions-takeaways-lessons-stats-recap-every-game|title=NFL Week 5: Biggest questions, takeaways for every game|work=NFL Nation|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=October 8, 2024|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref> [[Fox Sports]],<ref>{{cite web|last=McKenna|first=Henry|url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nfl/qb-stock-market-week-6-its-not-joe-burrows-fault-jordan-loves|title= QB Stock Market Week 6: It's not Joe Burrow's fault. Is it Jordan Love's? |publisher=[[Fox Sports]]|date=October 8, 2024|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref> and ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'', among others.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cummings|first=Keith|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/broncos/news/russell-wilson-deep-ball-next-gen-stats|title=Russell Wilson's Deep-Ball Accuracy, Ranking Will Surprise Broncos Fans|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=June 5, 2023|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref> Next Gen Stats were also included in the ''[[Madden NFL 21]]'' video game.<ref name=BW>{{cite press release|url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20201118005841/en/EA-Sports-Madden-NFL-21-Unveils-Next-Generation-Gameplay-Fueled-by-Real-World-NFL-Player-Data|title= EA Sports Madden NFL 21 Unveils Next Generation Gameplay Fueled by Real-World NFL Player Data |agency=[[Business Wire]]|publisher=[[Electronic Arts]]|date=November 18, 2020|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref>

==Statistics tracked==
The following statistics are tracked by NGS:<ref name=NGS2024/><ref name=glossary>{{cite web|url=https://nextgenstats.nfl.com/glossary|title=Glossary|publisher=NFL Next Gen Stats|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref>
;Passing
*Time To Throw (TT)
*Average Completed Air Yards (CAY) and Average Intended Air Yards (IAY)
*Average Air Yards Differential (AYD)
*Longest Completed Air Distance (LCAD)
*Aggressiveness (AGG%)
*Air Yards to the Sticks (AYTS)
*Completion Probability
*Expected Completion Percentage (xCOMP)
*Completion Percentage Above Expectation (+/-){{efn|Also called Completion Percentage Over Expectation (or CPOE).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/next-gen-stats-intro-to-passing-score-metric|title= Next Gen Stats: Intro to Passing Score metric |work=Next Gen Stats|publisher=[[National Football League]]|date=January 13, 2022|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref>}}

;Rushing
*Efficiency (EFF)
*8+ Defenders in the Box (8+D%)
*Avg Time Behind Line Of Scrimmage (TLOS)

;Receiving
*Average Cushion (CUSH)
*Average Separation (SEP)
*Average Targeted Air Yards (TAY)
*% Share of Team's Air Yards (TAY%)
*[[Yards After Catch]] (YAC)
*Expected Yards After Catch (xYAC)
*YAC Above Expectation (+/-)
   
;Top Plays
*Fastest Ball Carriers
*Longest Plays (Ball Carriers)
*Fastest Sacks
*Longest Tackles

;Other
*Tackle Probability
*Offensive Shift and Motion Classification
